claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have a child or children that you're responsible for?** If yes, how many children are you asking about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do! I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and I'm wondering if I can still claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! To help determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions.

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?** For example, is he studying for A-levels, Scottish Highers, or similar qualifications at school or college?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in education at the moment. He finished school and isn't doing A-levels or anything like that right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask a follow-up question:

**Is Alex registered with the armed services for training, or is he enrolled in any approved vocational training programs?** And also, **when exactly did he turn 16, or if he's now 17, when did he leave full-time education?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's not registered with the armed services or doing any vocational training. He just turned 17 not long ago, and he left school earlier this year when he finished his GCSEs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have one more important question:

**Has Alex registered with a government-approved careers service or with Connexions (or the equivalent service in your area)?** This would typically involve registering for help finding work or training opportunities.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or Connexions yet. He's just been taking a bit of time to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: Once a young person reaches 16, Child Benefit can only continue until they turn 20 if they remain in approved full-time non-advanced education or training. Since Alex has left school after completing his GCSEs and is not currently:
- In full-time education (like A-levels)
- In approved training
- Registered with a careers service or Connexions

He doesn't meet the criteria for continued Child Benefit.

**However, there's something Alex could do:** If he registers with a careers service like Connexions, this may help extend your eligibility in certain circumstances. It might be worth exploring this option if he needs support in finding work or training opportunities. Additionally, if he decides to return to education or start an approved training course in the future, you may become eligible again.

I hope this helps clarify your situation. If you have any other questions, please feel free to ask.
